reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical ordinary volume, including dimension zero. Let W:E->R be C1 and assume exp(-W) volume-integrable. Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)), the actual normalized Gibbs probability exp(-W)/partition described in the approved full-space context. A separate positive-partition binder is not a displayed additional assumption.
For EVERY original real-linear partial operator D:Lp R 2 mu->partialLinear[R] Lp E 2 mu, assume D.IsClosable and exact original graph: for every scalar L2 a and vector L2 G, (a,G) is in D.graph iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real phi with a=phi mu-AE and G=gradient(phi) mu-AE. D.closure is the genuine same-graph closure operator on its actual submodule domain.
For EVERY actual scalar f:Lp R 2 mu satisfying integral f(x) dmu(x)=0, and EVERY epsilon:N->R with all epsilon_n>0 and Tendsto epsilon atTop0, both following conclusions hold:
(1) The actual standard representative x->f(x) is Integrable under mu.
(2) There exists ONE actual family u:N->D.closure.domain. For every n, this family satisfies ALL the following:
  for every v:D.closure.domain,
    epsilon_n*<u_n,v>_{L2(mu;R)}+<D.closure(u_n),D.closure(v)>_{L2(mu;E)}=<f,v>_{L2(mu;R)};
  the standard scalar representative of u_n and actual standard vector representative of D.closure(u_n) are each locally integrable with respect to ordinary volume;
  for every real C1 compactly supported psi and every direction a:E, BOTH x->psi(x)*<D.closure(u_n)(x),a>_E and x->u_n(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable, and
    integral psi(x)*<D.closure(u_n)(x),a>_E dx = - integral u_n(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
For this SAME family, epsilon_n scalar-multiplied by (u_n as scalar L2(mu)) tends atTop to the zero quotient strongly in genuine weighted L2 norm topology.
D precedes all centered forcing and all sequences. One family is selected after f/epsilon and before every n and every test. Forcing L1 and mean, all variational inner products and limit use actual mu; local integrability and ordinary weak-gradient products/integrals use volume. Actual L2 quotients and standard measurable representatives are retained. There is no monotonicity or centered-u assumption. Only scaled-function convergence is explicitly concluded here, not scaled-gradient convergence, C2 PDE/cutoff facts or an unscaled/range/epsilon=0/further inequality/core/main/cost composition theorem. There is no joint measurable selector.
